#553: drill_hole is now a queued, vehicle-gated action -- a driller physically drives a drill_rig to each hole -- so this file (which pre-#553 never needed a driller at all) now needs one. campaign start has no staffed:true equivalent, so this is a manual hire + purchase, same pattern as weather-flood.json/vibration-budget.json. Employee #2 -- #1 is the surveyor hired above.

Left unmarked: hiring already grants blasting at Rookie (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION), but no role starts with driving.drill_rig -- without it the driller could never staff the drill_rig just bought. The player-facing path is training at a driving_center; skipped here since this file isn't about training.

#553 follow-up: a single driller/drill_rig cannot finish this 9-hole grid before well-being's 120-tick worker-revolt countdown completes -- sandbox-measured directly (pure command-mode engine probe, no browser): one driller starting fresh at tick 0 with full needs still only reaches 5/9 holes by the tick the crew revolts, and a `build living_quarters` early makes it WORSE (the driller detours to rest there instead of progressing, landing 0/9 holes). A second driller/drill_rig running in parallel is the strategy that actually finishes in time -- sandbox-measured landing at tick ~297 vs. revolt's tick ~333, an 8-tick margin at the tick-block sizes below. Employee #3 -- #1 is the surveyor, #2 the first driller, both hired above.
Left unmarked: same reasoning as employee #2's driving.drill_rig assignment above -- no role starts with this skill, and this file isn't about training.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:2 cols:2 spacing:2 depth:6 start:25,25
steps.description: depth corrected from 8 to 6 (Ground rule #15/Finding #42's class, the whole-suite audit before Phase 3): this step never clicks the grid tool's depth stepper (data-field="depth"), so the real drag always produces the panel's own 6m default regardless of what's declared. This file's own expect blocks only assert hole/charge/sequence counts around the affected blast (depth-insensitive), so this is a metadata-only correction -- verified both modes still pass unchanged. #553: spacing tightened from 5m to 2m to keep this 9-hole grid's drilling time reasonable, now with two drillers/drill_rigs working it in parallel. #554-followup (issue #586 CI, real failure): shrunk further from 9 holes (3x3) to 4 (2x2) -- real interaction-mode CI proved this file's own wellBeing (pinned at 0 with no living_quarters anywhere in the file, ScoreManager.ts's applyDecay deliberately keeps a score at exactly 0 there until direct intervention, per level1-lose-revolt.integration.test.ts's own documented design) crosses REVOLT_TICKS (120 consecutive ticks at 0, WorkerRevolt.ts) before the file's own player-facing sequence/blast steps can run once charging (#554: real, queued work, not instant) is added on top of drilling's own already-tight ~300-tick budget -- command mode's identical trace revolts too (sandbox-confirmed via direct state inspection: `revolted:true` by tick ~305-310 in both modes), it just never surfaced there because command mode has no DOM for the revolt's level-end overlay to block. Not a timing/chunking bug like the sibling fixes elsewhere this session -- the crew's own wellbeing budget was already spent by the time #554's charging needed it. 9 holes with 2 parallel drillers left ~40 real ticks of charging work needed past a ~305-tick deadline; 4 holes cuts both drilling and charging time roughly in half, landing comfortably inside the deadline instead of gambling the margin closer.

#553 follow-up: drain the ordered plan in bounded chunks rather than one large tick count -- each chunk is followed by `event choose 0` since a `tick` command stops dead the instant a timer event fires mid-block (events.ts), silently short of the requested count. #554-followup (issue #586 CI, real failure): this file's own wellBeing pins at exactly 0 partway through drilling (no living_quarters anywhere in the file) and ScoreManager.ts's applyDecay deliberately never lets a score at exactly 0 climb back up on its own (level1-lose-revolt.integration.test.ts documents this as intentional) -- so once REVOLT_TICKS (120 consecutive ticks at 0, WorkerRevolt.ts) elapses, revolt is unavoidable regardless of what commands run next. Sandbox-confirmed this file's original 9-hole/6-chunk drilling wait plus the charge-drain wait below already crossed that deadline in BOTH modes (`revolted:true` by tick ~305-310) -- command mode's own scenario-test run never surfaced it because it has no DOM for the revolt's level-end overlay to block, only interaction mode's real click on the sequence step below does. Shrinking the grid from 9 holes to 4 (see the drill_plan step's own note) was the real fix; trimmed from 6 chunks (225 nominal ticks, 75 of them dead padding past actual completion) to 3 -- sandbox-measured, 4 holes with two parallel drillers land exactly here, comfortably inside the revolt deadline instead of padding into it.

#554-followup round 2 (issue #586 CI): the earlier fix here (a real-time waitUntil, then 6 chunked tick-10/event-choose-0 rounds sized for the original 9-hole grid) treated this as a timing/convergence problem, but sandbox-inspection of live game state proved both modes actually revolt around tick ~305-310 regardless -- this file's own wellBeing pins at exactly 0 partway through drilling (no living_quarters anywhere in the file) and ScoreManager.ts's applyDecay deliberately never lets a score at exactly 0 recover on its own (level1-lose-revolt.integration.test.ts documents this as intentional design, not a bug), so once REVOLT_TICKS (120 consecutive ticks at 0) elapses, revolt is unavoidable no matter how the remaining ticks are chunked. The drill_plan step's own note has the real fix (9 holes -> 4), which lands drilling with real margin before the deadline; trimmed this charge-drain to match -- sandbox-measured, 4 holes charge in 20 ticks from here, comfortably inside the deadline instead of the original 60-tick budget that used to pad straight through it.
